decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom represents heavy development investment and a publicly announced strategic push into proton therapy QA, so any slow uptake would be attributed to long hospital procurement cycles and pandemic delays rather than product weakness.

Having already withdrawn the overlapping Product B, management has effectively chosen C as its small-volume chamber and would defend that choice by keeping it, even though some portfolio consolidation risk remains.
The multi-model standard clinical chamber line is core to the firm's established dosimetry and accredited calibration business, so dropping it is very unlikely.
The relative dosimetry chamber is tied into the firm's water phantom and connected QA workflow direction, so it remains strategically aligned and worth retaining.
Thimble chambers are staple reference instruments with steady demand and calibration-service linkage, so the firm continues to support the product.
